entries.name: ADPGK:Mg2+ phosphorylates Glc to G6P
entries.summation: Glucose phosphorylation is a central event in cellular metabolism. ADP-dependent glucokinase (ADPGK) can phosphorylate glucose (Glc) using ADP as the phosphate donor to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P). To date, it has not been established whether this phosphorylation supports a significant role in priming glucose for a metabolic fate other than glycolysis (Richter et al. 2012). Studies of metabolic changes during T cell activation suggest a role for it there (Kaminski et al. 2012).

entries.name: TP53 binds the TIGAR gene
entries.summation: TIGAR gene possesses two TP53 (p53) binding sites, one upstream of the first exon and another within the first intron. TP53 can bind both sites, with a higher affinity for the intronic site (Bensaad et al. 2006).

entries.name: PKM and TGIF2 repress CDH1 gene transcription
entries.summation: Pyruvate kinase PKM (also known as PKM2) and TGF-beta-induced transcription factor 2 (TGIF2) form a complex that directly represses the CDH1 gene transcription (Hamabe et al. 2014; Yang et al. 2022). The complex of PKM and TGIF2 at the CDH1 promoter may include histone deacetylase HDAC3 (Hamabe et al. 2014) and a Protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 26 (PPP1R26) (Yang et al. 2022).
